primitives.name: Deployment Gate Collapse
primitives.verbatim_quote: FINDING: `main` is completely unprotected, and 14 installed apps can write to it Independently re-verified: ``` gh api repos/Beexly/Sports/branches/main/protection -> 404 "Branch not protected" gh api repos/Beexly/Sports/rulesets -> [] gh api repos/Beexly/Sports/hooks -> 1 live webhook (Codacy) ``` **Why this is the headline.** Vercel auto-deploys `main` to Production.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'N_{apps}': 'dimensionless count of installed GitHub Apps with write access', 'P_{deploy}': 'probability of unauthorized production deploy'}
primitives.assumptions: Main branch is directly target of auto-deploy; 14 apps independently hold write permissions.

layer2.mapping: The kernel of system instability arises from absence of mandatory pull request enforcement on main branch, enabling any of 14 apps to trigger immediate production deployment.
layer2.telemetry: Number of apps with contents=write permission

primitives.name: Operational Nullity
primitives.verbatim_quote: FINDING: GitHub Actions are 100% failing on a billing block Last 100 runs: **100 failures**.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'F_{actions}': 'fraction of failed CI jobs', 'T_{run}': 'time interval between job initiation and runner assignment'}
primitives.assumptions: All CI jobs fail due to resource allocation blockage; no execution occurs.

layer2.mapping: The kernel of system nonfunctionality stems from complete CI pipeline halt, rendering all automated checks and deployments inert.
layer2.telemetry: Percentage of GitHub Actions jobs returning runner_id: 0

primitives.name: Third-Party Attack Surface
primitives.verbatim_quote: This is not "a vendor might be evil." It is: a compromise at ANY of ~14 third-party vendors becomes a production deploy with no gate.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'S_{surface}': 'total number of third-party integrations with write capability', 'R_{risk}': 'risk of unauthorized deployment from compromised vendor'}
primitives.assumptions: Each app with write access is a potential attack vector; no isolation exists between apps.

layer2.mapping: The supply chain surface mirrors the logical structure of a distributed denial-of-service attack, where each compromised app acts as a node capable of triggering system-wide failure.
layer2.telemetry: Count of installed GitHub Apps with elevated permissions

This creates a combinatorial risk space where any single compromised entity can lead to unauthorized production deployment. The mathematical model treats this as a probabilistic event space with 14 independent variables, each contributing to a cumulative risk function P_deploy = 1 - ∏(1 - p_i), where p_i is the probability of compromise for each app. Simultaneously, the GitHub Actions pipeline is fully disabled, indicating a systemic failure in infrastructure provisioning rather than logic. This renders all CI-based security controls ineffective, creating a dual failure mode: both unauthorized access and operational nullity. The supply chain surface expands beyond the repository to encompass all third-party integrations, forming a network of interdependent vulnerabilities. The failure manifests as a topological collapse of the deployment graph, where the main branch becomes a singular point of entry with no protective barriers.
